key_insight: A rotating superfluid helium vortex lattice supports deformation waves that behave as inertial waves at low frequencies and likely Kelvin-wave cascades at higher frequencies under heat-flux forcing.
engineering_relevance: The study gives a direct experimental window into collective wave dynamics in quantized vortices, informing models of turbulence and wave transport in rotating quantum fluids.
method: Prepare a regular quantum vortex lattice in rotating superfluid $^4$He.
Apply a constant heat flux to perturb the lattice and excite wave motion.
Visualize and analyze the resulting vortex deformation waves across frequency bands.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports observed continuous-frequency wave spectra below twice the rotation rate, matching inertial-wave structure, and higher-frequency signatures consistent with a Kelvin-wave turbulent cascade.
watch_item: The higher-frequency Kelvin-wave interpretation is presented as supporting evidence rather than definitive proof, so spectral attribution should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Visualization of Inertial and Kelvin Waves on the Quantum Vortex Lattice in Superfluid Helium
